tags.name: dois
tags.description: DOIs

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Search [DOI metadata fields](https://support.datacite.org/docs/api-queries#using-the-query-parameter) using OpenSearch query string syntax.

parameters.name: created
parameters.description: Filter by the DOI date created (yyyy). Use commas to filter by multiple years (yyyy,yyyy).

parameters.name: registered
parameters.description: Filter by the DOI date registered (yyyy). Use commas to filter by multiple years (yyyy,yyyy).

parameters.name: published
parameters.description: Filter by the DOI date published (yyyy). Use commas to filter by multiple years (yyyy,yyyy).

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: Filter by a specific prefix. Use commas to include multiple prefixes.

parameters.name: enriched
parameters.description: Retrieve, query, and filter [enriched DOI metadata](https://support.datacite.org/docs/metadata-enrichments) if available.

parameters.name: affiliation-id
parameters.description: Search creators.affiliation.affiliationIdentifier and contributors.affiliation.affiliationIdentifier for a ROR ID.

parameters.name: affiliation-country
parameters.description: Filter DOIs by associated country inferred from ROR IDs in creators/contributors affiliations. Use comma-separated ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes.

parameters.name: funded-by
parameters.description: Search fundingReferences.funderIdentifier for a ROR ID. Results also include DOIs containing a Crossref Funder ID in fundingReferences.funderIdentifier corresponding to the ROR ID.

parameters.name: include-funder-child-organizations
parameters.description: When the `funded-by=` parameter is set to a ROR ID and `include-funder-child-organizations=true`, the returned list of DOIs will be filtered to DataCite resources funded by the organization identified by the ROR ID as well as all of its child organizations. Child organizations include direct descendants as well as children of children.

parameters.name: funder-id
parameters.description: Search fundingReferences.funderIdentifier for a Crossref Funder ID.

parameters.name: user-id
parameters.description: Search creators.nameIdentifiers.nameIdentifier for an ORCID iD.

parameters.name: resource-type-id
parameters.description: Filter by the resourceTypeGeneral. Use commas to include multiple values.

parameters.name: resource-type
parameters.description: Filter by the free text resourceType. Use commas to include multiple values.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Filter by the free text Subject. Use commas to include multiple terms.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Filter by the [DOI state](https://support.datacite.org/docs/doi-states). Authentication is required to retrieve registered DOIs and draft records.

parameters.name: has-citations
parameters.description: Search the citationCount field for integer values greater than or equal to the inputted value.

parameters.name: has-references
parameters.description: Search the referenceCount field for integer values greater than or equal to the inputted value.

parameters.name: has-parts
parameters.description: Search the partCount field for integer values greater than or equal to the inputted value.

parameters.name: has-part-of
parameters.description: Search the partOfCount field for integer values greater than or equal to the inputted value.

parameters.name: has-versions
parameters.description: Search the versionCount field for integer values greater than or equal to the inputted value.

parameters.name: has-version-of
parameters.description: Search the versionOfCount field for integer values greater than or equal to the inputted value.

parameters.name: has-views
parameters.description: Search the viewCount field for integer values greater than or equal to the inputted value.

parameters.name: has-downloads
parameters.description: Search the downloadCount field for integer values greater than or equal to the inputted value.

parameters.name: has-person
parameters.description: Return DOIs where creators.nameIdentifiers.nameIdentifierScheme has at least one "ORCID" value.

parameters.name: has-affiliation
parameters.description: Return DOIs where either creators.affiliation.affiliationIdentifierScheme or contributors.affiliation.affiliationIdentifierScheme has at least one "ROR" value.

parameters.name: has-organization
parameters.description: Return DOIs where either creators.nameIdentifiers.nameIdentifierScheme or contributors.nameIdentifiers.nameIdentifierScheme has at least one "ROR" value.

parameters.name: has-funder
parameters.description: Return DOIs where fundingReferences.funderIdentifierType has at least one "Crossref Funder ID" value.

parameters.name: random
parameters.description: Retrieve a random sample of DOIs. When true, the `page[number]` parameter is ignored.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
Sort order:
 * `relevance` - Relevance score descending 
 * `name` - DOI name alphabetical ascending 
 * `-name` - DOI name alphabetical descending
 * `created` - Created date ascending
 * `-created` - Created date descending
 * `updated` - Updated date ascending
 * `-updated` - Updated date descending
 * `published` - Published date ascending
 * `-published` - Published date descending
 * `view-count` - viewCount ascending
 * `-view-count` - viewCount descending
 * `download-count` - downloadCount ascending
 * `-download-count` - downloadCount descending
 * `citation-count` - citationCount ascending
 * `-citation-count` - citationCount descending
 * `title` - first title alphabetical ascending
 * `-title` - first title alphabetical descending

parameters.name: disable-facets
parameters.description: Exclude facets from the response.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description:
When set to `true`, will include the following in the response:
 * attributes:
   * `prefix`
   * `suffix`
   * `viewsOverTime`
   * `citationsOverTime`
   * `references`
   * `citations`
   * `parts`
   * `partOf`
   * `versions`
   * `versionOf`
   * `xml`
   * `alternateIdentifiers`
* relationships:
   * `provider`

parameters.name: fields[dois]
parameters.description: Only return the attributes specified. For example, `fields[dois]=titles,subjects` will only return titles and subjects.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: The [system used to create the DOI](https://support.datacite.org/docs/api-get-doi#source).

event.description:
Can be set to trigger a [DOI state change](https://support.datacite.org/docs/updating-metadata-with-the-rest-api#changing-the-doi-state). When not set, a [Draft record](https://support.datacite.org/docs/doi-states#draft-record) is created.

  * `hide` - Change a DOI from Findable to Registered state.

ApiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyAuth.description: API key for authentication. Get your key from the API Keys page.

url.description: Original requested URL

description.description: Page meta description
description.example: This domain is for use in illustrative examples.

format.description: Format of the extracted text

text.description: Extracted content (string for markdown/html, object for json). Null if extraction failed.

links.description: Extracted links (only if links=true in request)

image_links.description: Extracted image links (only if image_links=true in request)

iframe_links.description: Extracted <iframe src> URLs, absolute and deduplicated (only if iframe_links=true in request)

page_metadata.description: Page-head metadata (only if page_metadata=true in request): canonical, favicon, robots, generator, viewport, keywords, plus nested og/twitter/article objects keyed by tag suffix and remaining named meta tags under `other`. Tags that legitimately repeat (og:image, og:locale:alternate, article:tag, article:author) collect into arrays. Keys are omitted when the page does not declare them; the whole field is omitted when the page exposes none.

latency_ms.description: Fetch latency for this URL in milliseconds if available from tf-fetch

not_modified.description: Present and `true` only when the origin returned 304 Not Modified for your `if_none_match`/`if_modified_since`; omitted otherwise.

etag.description: The origin's current ETag validator, present only when the origin sent one and you set `include_etag_and_last_modified: true`; omitted otherwise. Store it and replay it as `if_none_match`.

last_modified.description: The origin's current Last-Modified validator, present only when the origin sent one and you set `include_etag_and_last_modified: true`; omitted otherwise. Store it and replay it as `if_modified_since`.

unmatched_selectors.description: Partial-miss report for `include_selectors`: the entries that matched no elements on this page, present only when some (but not all) entries matched — the result still carries the matched content. Omitted when every entry matched. A total miss is not a result at all: it is reported as a `selector_not_matched` entry in `errors[]`.

results.description: Successfully fetched URLs

url.description: URL that failed to fetch

error.description: Error code describing the failure. Possible values: `target_http_error` (target server returned a non-2xx HTTP status other than 404/410 — see `status` field), `page_not_found` (target returned HTTP 404 or 410), `target_unreachable` (connection refused, TLS failure, or network error), `timeout` (request timed out), `proxy_error` (proxy tunnel failure), `bot_blocked` (bot-challenge page detected), `empty_content` (page loaded but no extractable text), `login_required` (target redirected to a login or account wall; the page is not served to anonymous sessions, so retrying without credentials will not help), `content_too_large` (document exceeds the 20MB size limit for generic documents — not retried in the browser; PDF and CSV have their own 50MB budgets), `invalid_url` (malformed URL or SSRF-blocked address), `invalid_redirect_url` (redirect target rejected before fetch), `conditional_unsupported` (conditional requests are supported on the fast path only; this URL requires browser rendering), `selector_not_matched` (no elements matching any `include_selectors` entry remained after `exclude_selectors` was applied — a total miss; carries `unmatched_selectors` and `candidate_selectors` retry hints. A partial miss is NOT an error: it is reported via the result's `unmatched_selectors`), `selector_unsupported` (`include_selectors`/`exclude_selectors` sent for a URL that resolves to a direct PDF/CSV download — no HTML to scope).

status.description: Upstream HTTP status code. Only present when `error` is `target_http_error` or `page_not_found`.

unmatched_selectors.description: The `include_selectors` entries that matched no elements on the fetched page. Only present when `error` is `selector_not_matched`.

candidate_selectors.description: Cheap retry hints (max 10), only present when `error` is `selector_not_matched`: landmark tags present on the page (e.g. `main`, `article`, `nav`) plus `#id` selectors of content-heavy elements. Retry the fetch with `include_selectors` drawn from this list.

items.description: A URL that failed to fetch

request_id.description: Request correlation ID, also returned as the X-Request-ID response header. Present only when errors is non-empty; include it when reporting failed URLs.

is_baseline.description: True for the first run; nothing to compare.

url.description: Result URL

thumbnail_url.description: Thumbnail image URL, present only when include_thumbnail=true and a thumbnail is available

fetch.description: Fetched page content, present only when fetch param is supplied

fetch_error.description: Fetch error details when fetch was requested. Contains details on failure; may be null when fetching succeeds.

date.description: Publication date, present for news and some web results

publisher.description: Publisher name, present for news results when domain_type=news

authors.description: Author list, present for academic results when domain_type=research_paper

venue.description: Journal or conference name, present when domain_type=research_paper

pdf_url.description: PDF URL, present when domain_type=research_paper and a PDF is available

items.description: A single search result

post.description:
Creates and enqueues multiple automation runs in a single request, returning run_ids immediately without waiting for completion. Maximum 100 runs per request.

**Atomic creation:** Run creation is all-or-nothing. Either all runs are created successfully, or none are (returns error).

**Idempotency:** This endpoint does not currently support idempotency keys. Retrying a failed request may create duplicate runs.

post.summary: Fetch and extract content from URLs
post.description:
Fetches web pages, renders JavaScript-heavy pages when needed, and returns clean extracted content in your preferred format. Submit up to 10 URLs, get back structured content. Per-URL failures appear in `errors[]` and do not fail the entire request.

**Per-URL error codes** (in `errors[].error`):
- `target_http_error` — target server returned a non-2xx HTTP status other than 404/410; the raw status code is in `errors[].status`
- `page_not_found` — target URL returned HTTP 404 or 410; the raw status code is in `errors[].status`
- `target_unreachable` — connection refused, TLS failure, DNS failure, or other network error
- `timeout` — request timed out
- `proxy_error` — proxy tunnel failure
- `bot_blocked` — bot-challenge page detected (Cloudflare, etc.)
- `empty_content` — page loaded but no extractable text was found
- `login_required` — the target redirected to a login or account wall; retrying without credentials will not help
- `content_too_large` — the document exceeds the 20MB size limit for generic documents (PDF and CSV have their own 50MB budgets); not retried in the browser
- `invalid_url` — malformed URL or SSRF-blocked address
- `invalid_redirect_url` — redirect target rejected before fetch
- `conditional_unsupported` — conditional requests (`if_none_match` / `if_modified_since`) are supported on the fast path only; this URL requires browser rendering
- `selector_not_matched` — no elements matching any `include_selectors` entry remained after `exclude_selectors` was applied; the error carries `unmatched_selectors` plus `candidate_selectors` retry hints (a partial miss is not an error — it's reported on the result's `unmatched_selectors`)
- `selector_unsupported` — `include_selectors` / `exclude_selectors` sent for a URL that resolves to a direct PDF/CSV download (no HTML to scope)

requestBody.description: URLs to fetch and extraction options

urls.description: Array of URLs to fetch (1-10). All URLs are fetched in parallel. Each URL is processed independently — if one fails, others still return successfully. Errors are reported per-URL in the errors array.

purpose.description: Why these URLs are being fetched — the underlying goal or task the content will be used for. Used to better tailor fetching and extraction to your intent.
purpose.example: Compare pricing tiers across vendors for a procurement report

format.description: Output format for extracted content. "markdown" (default) is ideal for LLM consumption. "html" returns cleaned semantic HTML. "json" returns a structured document tree.

links.description: Extract all outbound links (<a href>) from each page. Useful for discovering related pages or navigating to specific content. Links are returned as absolute URLs in the links array of each result.

image_links.description: Extract all image URLs () from each page. Useful for finding visual content or media assets. Image links are returned as absolute URLs in the image_links array of each result.

iframe_links.description: Extract the src URLs of <iframe> elements on each page. Useful when a page embeds its main content in a frame (job boards, booking widgets, document viewers): fetch the returned URL to read the embedded content. Iframe links are returned as absolute, deduplicated URLs in the iframe_links array of each result. Script-injected iframes are only present when the page was rendered in a browser.

page_metadata.description: Return page-head metadata for each page in the page_metadata object of each result: canonical URL, favicon, robots directive, generator, viewport, keywords, all Open Graph (og), Twitter card (twitter), and article tags, and remaining named meta tags under `other`. Useful for SEO/technical audits and link-preview generation.

ttl.description: Caller freshness tolerance in seconds for the cached entry. Omit (default) for unlimited tolerance — any cached entry is acceptable. Set to 0 to prefer a live fetch; a cached entry is still served if the origin's Cache-Control: max-age covers its age, or the host is in the small allowlist of operator-pinned never-expire domains. Set to N > 0 to accept a cached entry whose age is below N; the upstream Cache-Control: max-age and the never-expire allowlist may extend (never shorten) this tolerance.

per_url_timeout_ms.description: Wall-clock timeout budget in milliseconds applied independently to each URL. If one URL exceeds this budget, it returns a per-URL timeout error while other URLs in the same request continue.

if_none_match.description: ETag validator from a prior fetch of this URL, forwarded verbatim as the If-None-Match header on the origin request. Only valid with a single URL — combining with a batch of URLs returns a 400. tf-fetch does not persist validators; the caller owns replaying them.

if_modified_since.description: Last-Modified validator from a prior fetch of this URL, forwarded verbatim as the If-Modified-Since header on the origin request. Only valid with a single URL — combining with a batch of URLs returns a 400. tf-fetch does not persist validators; the caller owns replaying them.

include_etag_and_last_modified.description: Opt-in to receiving `etag` / `last_modified` validators (and `not_modified` detection) on each result. Defaults to false — tf-fetch omits these fields unless requested. Independent of `if_none_match` / `if_modified_since`: works with a single URL or a batch.

include_selectors.description: Array of CSS selectors (1-20 entries, each 1-1000 characters) that scope extracted content (`text`, `links`, `image_links`) to elements matching ANY entry, concatenated in document order. Tag selectors cover semantic sections (`main`, `article`, `nav`); entries may themselves use CSS comma-grouping. Selected content is returned verbatim in the requested format (scripts/styles stripped) — automatic boilerplate removal is bypassed. Page-level metadata (`title`, `description`, `language`, `author`, `published_date`) still comes from the full document. When some entries match and others do not, the URL still succeeds and the misses are reported in the result's `unmatched_selectors`. When no entry matches anything, that URL fails with the per-URL error code `selector_not_matched` (carrying `unmatched_selectors` and `candidate_selectors` retry hints) — never a silent full-page fallback. URLs that resolve to direct PDF/CSV downloads fail with `selector_unsupported`. Invalid CSS selector syntax is rejected with a 422. Applied post-fetch: caching and routing are unchanged.

exclude_selectors.description: Array of CSS selectors (1-20 entries, each 1-1000 characters) for elements to remove before extraction — applied before `include_selectors` scopes what remains, so it also prunes inside selected regions. post.description:
Creates a remote tf-browser session and returns CDP connection details. Connect to the browser via CDP WebSocket at `cdp_url`.

By default the session egresses through the TinyFish residential proxy in the US, pinned to one exit IP for the life of the session. Use `proxy_config` to pick another country (`country_code`, any ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), bring your own proxy (`type: "custom"`), or disable the proxy (`enabled: false`).

Use `timeout_seconds` to set a custom inactivity timeout (5–86400 seconds). If omitted, null, or greater than your plan maximum, the plan maximum is used (15 min on free tier, 60 min on paid).

url.description: Target URL the browser session will navigate to on startup. Bare domains (e.g. tinyfish.ai) are automatically prefixed with https://. If omitted, the browser starts at about:blank.

timeout_seconds.description: Inactivity timeout in seconds (5–86400). If omitted, null, or greater than your plan maximum, the plan maximum is used.

enabled.description: Route the session through a proxy. false means direct egress.

type.description: "tinyfish" uses the TinyFish residential proxy, pinned to one exit IP per session. "custom" routes through your own proxy — requires url.

country_code.description: Exit country for the TinyFish proxy (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). Defaults to US.

url.description: Your HTTP or HTTPS proxy server URL. Required when type is "custom".

proxy_config.description: Proxy for the session. Omit to use the TinyFish proxy in the US.

session_id.description: Unique identifier for this browser session.

cdp_url.description: WebSocket URL for browser connection. Pass this to Playwright's connect_over_cdp or any WebSocket-based CDP client.

base_url.description: HTTPS base URL for the session. Use to access session endpoints such as /pages.

schema.description: Browser session created successfully. Connect to the browser via cdp_url.

info.title: Elicit API
info.description:
The Elicit API lets you search academic papers and clinical trials, run research workflows, and manage your library and shared projects.

## Getting started

This reference documents **v2**, with production base URL `https://elicit.com/api/v2`. Paths below are relative to that base. The older v1 API uses different paths and response envelopes; do not mix v1 examples with this reference.

1. Use an Elicit account with API access (Pro or above) and create an API key in [account settings](https://elicit.com/settings).
2. Set `ELICIT_API_KEY` in your environment. Keep it secret; do not embed it in browser code or commit it to source control.
3. Make a search request:

```bash
curl --fail-with-body https://elicit.com/api/v2/search/papers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ELICIT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"effects of sleep deprivation on cognitive performance","maxResults":10}'
```

The response contains `papers` and may include non-fatal `warnings`; inspect warnings even on a successful response. Search returns results in the same request; research workflows return a session to poll instead.

### Choose an endpoint

| Goal | Start here |
|------|------------|
| Search papers or clinical trials | `POST /search/papers` or `POST /search/trials` |
| Generate a report from a question | `POST /sessions/reports` |
| Configure search, screening, extraction, and reporting stages | `POST /sessions/systematic-reviews` |
| Run interactive research with follow-up messages and artifacts | `POST /sessions/agents` |
| Find existing sessions or resume quota-paused work | `GET /sessions`; follow `links.self` or `links.resume` |
| Save papers, import PDFs, or organize collections | `/library/sources`, `/library/imports`, and `/library/collections` |
| Create, browse, or share projects | `POST /projects`, `GET /projects`, and `POST /projects/{projectId}/shares` |
| Schedule recurring Research Agent work | `/routines` |
| Check account usage | `GET /usage` |

## Authentication

All API requests require a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer elk_live_your_key_here
```

API keys can be created and managed from your [Elicit account settings](https://elicit.com/settings).

## Billing

API access requires a Pro plan or above. Your plan limits **results per search request**, not requests per day. Exceeding the plan's `maxResults` cap returns `400 invalid_request`; see the Search endpoints for the per-plan limits.

All endpoints share a burst limit of **100 requests per minute per IP address**, including polling requests. Exceeding it returns `429` and blocks that IP for **5 minutes**. Coordinate polling across concurrent sessions and clients behind the same IP.

An exhausted usage allowance returns `402 insufficient_quota` when starting work (`error.details.reason` is `credits_exhausted` or, for an organization member over the weekly limit set by their admin, `spend_limit_reached`; `error.details.resetsAt` is when the block lifts), or pauses a running session with `status: "pausedForInsufficientQuota"`. Check `GET /usage`, resolve the limit, then POST to `links.resume`; paused work does not automatically resume. Usage reporting can return `409` for accounts without usage reporting or while their usage data is not ready.

Manage your plan in [account settings](https://elicit.com/settings).

## Code Examples

Working examples in curl, Python, and JavaScript, plus integrations (CLI tool, Slack bot, Claude Code skill):

**[github.com/elicit/api-examples](https://github.com/elicit/api-examples)**

## Error Handling

Application errors use this JSON envelope. Branch on the HTTP status and `error.code`, not the wording of `error.message`:

```json
{"error":{"code":"invalid_request","message":"body.query: Required"}}
```

**Exception: the edge rate limit** returns a flat body, not an `error` object:

```json
{"error":"Rate limit exceeded","message":"Too many requests. Please try again later."}
```

| HTTP status | What to do |
|-------------|------------|
| `400` | Correct the body, query parameters, or path ID; consult the endpoint's error codes. |
| `401` | Supply a valid `Authorization: Bearer ...` header. |
| `402` | Resolve the account's usage limit before starting or resuming work. |
| `403` | Check plan eligibility and the permissions required for this operation. |
| `404` | Check the ID and access. Inaccessible resources can also return 404; see endpoint-specific codes for full-text availability. |
| `409` | Resolve the conflict described by `error.code`; do not retry blindly. |
| `410` | A staged upload expired; stage and upload the file again. |
| `429` | Stop requests from this IP for the 5-minute block, then reduce the request rate. |
| `5xx` | Retry reads with bounded exponential backoff and jitter. For writes, check whether the first request took effect before retrying. |

Creation and message requests are not guaranteed to be idempotent. A timeout does not prove that work was not started: retrying can create another session or submit another turn. Save returned IDs and use the read endpoints to check progress. Repeat a write only when the endpoint documents that it is safe or you have confirmed it did not take effect.

## Pagination and asynchronous work

Paginated session, source, collection, project, routine, and routine-run lists return `nextCursor`; most also return `totalCount`, while routine lists do not. Share lists and agent artifact/source lists are not paginated. Omit `cursor` for the first page; pass `nextCursor` unchanged as the next request's `cursor`, keeping the same filters and sort. Stop when it is `null`. Treat cursors as opaque and URL-encode them. Lists are not frozen snapshots of changing data.

```bash
curl --get https://elicit.com/api/v2/sessions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ELICIT_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=10" \
  --data-urlencode "cursor=$NEXT_CURSOR"
```

Creating a research session returns `202 Accepted`: work has been accepted, not finished. Store the `sessionId`. For reports and systematic reviews, follow `links.self` for API status; `url` opens the web interface. Poll reports and systematic reviews every 30–60 seconds. Stop normal polling on `completed`, `failed`, or `unknown`; handle `pausedForInsufficientQuota` separately as described above. Export downloads may lag behind the research: neither `completed` nor `exportsStatus: "ready"` guarantees a current export set. If expected URLs are missing, wait at least 60 seconds and fetch the detail endpoint again; use bounded retries with backoff rather than treating the omissions as final.

Research Agent sessions are interactive: `completed` means the agent is idle and can receive another message, not permanently closed. Use their events endpoint every 3–10 seconds while processing. Its `cursor` is an incremental activity checkpoint, **not** a list's `nextCursor`.

## MCP Server

Elicit also offers an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) (Model Context Protocol) server for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and other MCP-compatible clients. Authentication is via OAuth 2.0, rather than the REST API key shown above.

MCP exposes search, reports, systematic reviews, the Research Agent session lifecycle, routines, file-upload staging, artifact reads/downloads, session sharing, session listing/resumption, project creation/listing, usage, and library tools. It is **not a one-to-one mirror of this REST reference**: dedicated cited-source retrieval and project sharing remain REST capabilities without corresponding public MCP tools. Use your client's `tools/list` result as the authoritative MCP tool inventory. Tools for routines are shown only for accounts that can use them.

### Claude Code

```
claude mcp add --transport http elicit https://elicit.com/api/mcp
```

Then run `/mcp`, select the `elicit` server, and choose **Authenticate** to open a browser for login.

### Claude Desktop

**Via the UI:** Click the icon next to your name > **Settings** > **Connectors** > **Add custom connector**. Enter `Elicit` for the name and `https://elicit.com/api/mcp` for the URL.

### Research Agent workflow over MCP

Use an account with public API access (Pro or above), authenticated as the person who owns the session or has been explicitly granted read access. The same plan, quota, and session-access rules as REST apply. No API key or switch to REST is needed after the MCP OAuth connection is established. The new agent-specific tools are public-only. Elicit's private agentic MCP retains read-only session listing but cannot create, message, stop, or resume Research Agent sessions, including through the generic resume tool.

| Tool | Arguments | Result / next step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create_agent_session` | `query` (1–20000 characters), optional `researchDepth` (`fastest`, `fast`, `balanced`, `smart`, `smartest`), optional `attachments: [{file_id}]`, optional `projectId` | Save `sessionId` and `url`; initial status is `processing`. |
| `list_sessions` | Optional `type: "agent"`, `status`, `source`, `limit`, `cursor` | Find owned or explicitly shared sessions. `role: "shared"` means read-only. Use `nextCursor` for the next list page. |
| `get_agent_session` | `sessionId` | Inspect status and the link to open in Elicit. |
| `get_agent_session_events` | `sessionId`, optional `cursor` | Read conversation, progress, answers, citations, and Methods incrementally. |
| `send_agent_session_message` | `sessionId`, `message` (1–20000 characters), optional `attachments: [{file_id}]` | Returns a `messageId` matching the resulting `user_message` event. Owner only. |
| `stop_agent_session` | `sessionId` | Safely repeat if needed. `stopping` acknowledges a queued request; wait for `session_stopped`. Owner only; allowed even with exhausted quota. |
| `resume_session` | `sessionId` | Resume quota-paused work once eligible; check `get_usage` if quota is still insufficient. Owner only. |

**Example in Claude Code or Claude Desktop:** ask “Start a Research Agent session on exercise and cardiovascular outcomes. Save its ID and URL, follow its progress, and show me the answer with citations and Methods.” After it is idle, ask “In that same session, compare the randomized trials.” To interrupt the new turn, ask “Stop that session and confirm it has stopped.” To find older work, ask “List my Research Agent sessions”; to resume eligible work, ask “Resume my quota-paused Research Agent session.” Refresh the client's tool list if it cached an older connection.

**Status:** `processing` means working; `completed` means idle and ready for input, not permanently closed; `failed` cannot accept another message; `pausedForInsufficientQuota` requires quota and `resume_session` before another message. A stopped turn is identified by the `session_stopped` event (or `stopped` from the stop tool), not a distinct status in list/detail/events responses. It can accept a new message. Prefer sending follow-ups after `session_idle` / `completed`. The API may also accept a message while an agentic turn is running; a legacy running session can return `session_processing`.

**Incremental polling and reconnects:** omit the events cursor only on the first read. Consume the entire returned page, then save its opaque `cursor` alongside the session ID and pass it unchanged on the next call. Poll with a delay (for example, five seconds); an empty page is not completion. If interrupted, reconnect and retry from the last consumed checkpoint. Deduplicate replayed events by `eventId`; later snapshots with the same `messageId` replace earlier snapshots for display. Do not confuse the events cursor with the list cursor, decode it, or reuse it for another session. The unchanged REST event representation preserves citation references and source metadata, as well as `methods` events. The endpoint uses ordinary JSON tool responses, not SSE or background notifications; the assistant may need a prompt to continue polling after it ends a conversational turn.

**Access and errors:** shared users can list and read but cannot send messages, stop, or resume; a public URL alone does not grant API read access. Tool failures return `isError: true` with an actionable message and code: `invalid_arguments` (correct the fields), `api_access_denied` (upgrade the account), `session_not_found` (check the ID and explicit share), `insufficient_quota` (replenish quota), `session_paused` (resume first), `session_failed` (start a new session), or `session_not_paused` (inspect current status). For `invalid_cursor`, `cursor_session_mismatch`, or `cursor_out_of_range`, check the saved session/checkpoint; if it cannot be recovered, omit the cursor and rebuild from full history. Authentication failures require reconnecting or authenticating again.

**Client timeouts:** creation and control operations can take tens of seconds; clients should allow at least 60 seconds per tool call. A client timeout is not proof a mutation failed. Creation and messages are not idempotent: inspect `list_sessions` or session events before retrying to avoid duplicate work. If initialization may have committed, a creation error includes a typed `sessionId` recovery field: REST returns `{error: {code, message, sessionId}}`; MCP returns `isError: true` with the JSON object `{code, message, sessionId}` in `content[0].text` (no success `structuredContent`). Parse the JSON field, not the prose. Inspect that session rather than starting a replacement; its attachment claims remain bound to it. A late initialization failure is reconciled: if no initial event committed, the session and claims are rolled back and subsequent reads return `session_not_found`, after which creation can be retried. Persisted or uncertain outcomes remain preserved. Stops may be retried safely. MCP-created sessions record `source: "mcp"`, and lifecycle analytics retain MCP attribution.

### Projects over MCP

Call `list_projects({})` to find an existing project with `role: "owner"`, or `create_project({name: "GLP-1 safety review", goal: "Compare cardiovascular outcomes"})` to create one. Then call `create_agent_session({query: "Compare the latest trials", projectId: "<returned project id>"})`. The session is added to the project before research begins, and the initial turn receives that project context. The response includes `projectId`.

Only owned projects are supported for session creation; reader and writer shares do not qualify. Omit `projectId` to keep the existing standalone behavior. These project tools are public-only. Project creation and session creation are separate, non-idempotent operations: keep the project id for later sessions, and check `list_projects({consistency: "strong"})` before considering a retry of timed-out project creation. Routine listing defaults to reader-backed eventual consistency; strong recovery reads use the writer. Keep the same consistency when paginating. A failed session creation does not delete the project.

### Files, artifacts, and sharing over MCP

These resource tools are public-only and reuse REST permissions and limits. Existing private MCP library tools, including `stage_library_upload`, are unchanged; the new tools do not let the internal agent read or manage other Research Agent sessions. Upload, artifact, and share analytics record the MCP surface.

| Tool | Arguments | Result / next step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stage_file_upload` | `filename`, `content_type`, `size_bytes` | Returns `file_id`, `upload_url`, `expires_at`. Transfer bytes before attaching the file. |
| `get_agent_session_artifacts` | `sessionId` | Lists latest file-backed `artifacts` and interactive `deliveredOutputs`, using the delivery envelope below. |
| `get_agent_session_artifact_content` | `sessionId`, `artifactId` | Structured content of a delivered output, including citations, using the delivery envelope below. |
| `download_agent_session_artifact` | `sessionId`, `artifactId`, optional `format` | `original` (default) for file-backed artifacts; `json` for any delivered output; `csv`/`xlsx` for tables; `md` for prose. Returns `downloadUrl`, `expiresAt`, `filename`, `contentType`. |
| `create_session_share` | `sessionId`, `email` | Owner-only read-only grant or invitation for an agent session, report, or systematic review. May send email; approve the recipient first. Existing higher permissions are preserved. |
| `list_session_shares` | `sessionId` | Owner-only list of read-only recipients and invitations; editors/reviewers are omitted. |
| `delete_session_share` | `sessionId`, `email` | Owner-only, idempotent revocation of any direct role or invitation, including editor/reviewer access omitted from the list. Other access paths are unaffected. |

**Complete example with Claude Code:** connect and authenticate as above, then ask: “Use the local file trial-results.pdf as evidence for a Research Agent comparison of these trials. Stage and upload the file, start research with its file_id, save the session ID and URL, and follow progress using the returned cursor. Show the answer with citations and Methods. Once idle, attach follow-up.pdf in a follow-up asking for a comparison table and a prose summary. Retrieve the structured table and download CSV, XLSX, and Markdown exports to local files. Ask me before sharing the session with colleague@example.com, then list the shares. Start a further analysis, stop it while it is working, and confirm session_stopped.”

The concrete sequence is:

1. Compute the exact local file size; call `stage_file_upload({filename: "trial-results.pdf", content_type: "application/pdf", size_bytes: <bytes>})`.
2. PUT the bytes to the returned URL. For a shell-capable client, use the command below; it must succeed before continuing. Never send the Elicit OAuth bearer token to this URL.
3. Call `create_agent_session({query: "Compare these trials", attachments: [{file_id: "<returned UUID>"}]})`. Poll `get_agent_session_events({sessionId, cursor})` as above. Staging alone does not attach anything.
4. After idle, stage/upload the second file and call `send_agent_session_message({sessionId, message: "Compare these studies in a table and prose summary", attachments: [{file_id: "<second UUID>"}]})`. Follow events using the saved cursor.
5. Call `get_agent_session_artifacts({sessionId})`. For a delivered table, call `get_agent_session_artifact_content({sessionId, artifactId})` and `download_agent_session_artifact({sessionId, artifactId, format: "csv"})` (or `xlsx`). For prose use `md`; for all delivered kinds use `json`. For a file-backed artifact omit the format. Always use the opaque IDs returned by the list, never a filename, URL, bucket, or key.
6. Fetch the returned download URL into a local file, without an Authorization header. For large JSON, inspect selected rows/fields outside model context instead of pasting the full file into chat. A successful tool call returns a link, not proof the client downloaded it.
7. With approval, call `create_session_share({sessionId, email: "colleague@example.com"})`, then `list_session_shares({sessionId})`. The authenticated recipient can read artifacts but cannot send, stop, resume, or manage shares. To revoke, call `delete_session_share` with the same arguments.
8. Call `stop_agent_session({sessionId})` during ongoing work and poll for `session_stopped`; repeating stop is safe.

```bash
# Use upload_url from stage_file_upload, not the MCP endpoint:
curl --fail --request PUT --upload-file trial-results.pdf \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/pdf' "$UPLOAD_URL"
# Use downloadUrl returned by a download tool (or the delivery envelope):
curl --fail --location "$DOWNLOAD_URL" --output research-output.csv
```

**Large results:** artifact listing and content tools return `{delivery: "inline", data: ...}` for small results. When the formatted JSON exceeds 24 KiB, they instead return `{delivery: "download", download: {downloadUrl, expiresAt, filename, contentType}, sizeBytes}`, linking to the complete JSON with no truncation. This avoids placing large tables/prose in MCP responses, including the duplicate text/structured representation. JSON exports are serialized incrementally with a streaming JSON dependency through a temporary file, yielding between chunks rather than building a second full in-memory copy of the response. Generated exports are limited to 64 MiB and return `artifact_too_large` rather than partial content. Each process allows at most four active JSON spools (256 MiB aggregate); excess requests return retryable `export_busy` instead of queueing unbounded work. Upload/signing has a 60-second deadline (`export_timeout` is retryable); unsuccessful exports are removed best-effort, and S3 bucket lifecycle expires current objects under `mcp/agent-artifacts/` after one day and noncurrent versions one day after becoming noncurrent, and cleans up expired delete markers. Lifecycle expiration is day-based and deletion is asynchronous, so stored bytes can remain longer; it is separate from the download URL expiry. Temporary local files are removed after success or failure. It does not paginate or silently omit rows, slides, citations, or metadata. Download links last 30 minutes; call the tool again for a fresh link. The next call may reflect newer session output, so retain the downloaded file if you need that snapshot.

**Transfer limits and client capabilities:** the 30 MiB per-file limit and the 100-file, 10GB-total session limits apply. Upload eligibility, ownership, exact size, expiry, and one-session-or-import claiming rules are unchanged. An already-attached file can be reused in the same session. Unclaimed files and PUT URLs expire after 30 minutes. Unsupported export formats return `invalid_arguments` or `download_not_available`; missing or inaccessible sessions/artifacts return `session_not_found` or `artifact_not_found`. Upload validation failures are returned as actionable tool errors; fix the upload before retrying the create/message.

Claude Code can use local file and HTTP tools, subject to its permissions. A remote MCP connector alone, including a chat-only Claude Desktop setup, does not give the server access to a local file or guarantee that the client can perform PUT/GET transfers. Such clients need a separate file-transfer capability or a user-performed transfer; do not claim end-to-end upload/download support without testing it in that client. Download URLs are temporary bearer capabilities: keep them private and use session sharing for durable access. Revoking a share prevents future authorized reads but cannot invalidate already-issued download URLs before expiry.

### Other MCP clients

Connect any MCP client using HTTP transport to `https://elicit.com/api/mcp`. OAuth discovery is available at `https://elicit.com/api/mcp/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`.

For MCP setup guides, tool reference, and usage examples, see [github.com/elicit/api-examples/tree/main/integrations/mcp](https://github.com/elicit/api-examples/tree/main/integrations/mcp).

tags.name: Search
tags.description: One-shot searches over papers and clinical trials.

tags.name: Sessions
tags.description: Long-running research sessions. Reports, systematic reviews, and Research Agent sessions are kinds of sessions; list and resume them uniformly here, or use the typed subsections to create them and fetch results.

tags.name: Reports
tags.description: Create reports and fetch their status and results.

tags.name: Systematic Reviews
tags.description: Create systematic reviews and fetch their status and results.

tags.name: Usage
tags.description: Report plan usage and extra usage — the account-settings usage meter, over the API.

tags.name: Research Agent
tags.description: Stateful research sessions with incremental activity, follow-up messages, file uploads, and downloadable artifacts. Owners and direct share recipients can read session details, events, sources, and artifacts; only owners can send messages, stop, resume, or manage shares.

tags.name: Routines
tags.description:
Schedule a recurring instruction against an existing Research Agent session, manage its lifecycle, inspect its run history, or request an immediate run.

### Conventions

- Routines are available to eligible Pro, Scale, and Enterprise accounts. A `403` response indicates whether API access or routines are unavailable.
- API keys act as their user. Session owners and editors can manage a routine; readers can list it, retrieve it, and inspect its runs. Only the routine owner can change `ownerNotificationLevel`.
- An inaccessible routine or session returns `404` so its existence is not disclosed.
- Schedules are daily or weekly in an IANA time zone. Pausing stops future scheduled occurrences; resuming restores the schedule. Archiving removes the schedule but preserves the routine and its run history. Restoring an archived routine leaves it paused, so call resume separately when it should run again.
- Creating, updating, resuming, or immediately running a routine can be refused when the attached session owner's plan does not include routines. Creation, resume, and immediate runs also require that owner to be able to run agent work. Pause, archive, and restore remain available to eligible managers.
- Each executed immediate run consumes an agent turn. Accepted requests may be skipped if another run starts before processing; skipped requests do not appear in run history. Only one manual request may be queued or running at a time; another request returns `409 routine_run_already_pending`.
- List cursors are opaque and bound to their filters and sort. Run-history cursors are also bound to the routine. Pass `nextCursor` back unchanged and stop when it is `null`.

tags.name: Library
tags.description:
Your library: saved papers (sources) and the collections that group them, including items shared with you.

### Conventions

- A detail endpoint returns the resource. A list endpoint returns `{ <items>, nextCursor, totalCount }`. Send `nextCursor` as `cursor` to get the next page. `nextCursor` is `null` on the last page.
- You see your own sources and collections plus any shared with you. Each carries your `role`. On a collection, `reader`, `writer`, or `owner`: readers view; writers also add and remove sources and edit the name and description; owners also delete it and change who it is shared with. On a source, `reader` or `writer`: writers edit its metadata, attach a PDF, delete it, and add it to collections.
- A shared collection owns its papers. Adding one of your sources to it copies the paper into the collection; your own source is unchanged, and you are a `writer` on the copy if you own or can edit the collection and a `reader` if you can only view it. Removing a paper from such a collection moves it to the collection's trash for 30 days.
- An id you cannot see returns `404`. An action your role does not allow returns `403 forbidden`.
- Creating a collection returns `201`; synchronous bulk operations return `200`; PDF imports return `202` and must be polled. Retry behavior varies by endpoint. Creating a collection again creates another collection, and saving sources with `onDuplicate: create` can create additional copies.
- A duplicate is not an error. Saving a paper that is already in your library returns the existing source with `created: false` and `duplicateOf` set; with `onDuplicate: create`, a copy is saved with `created: true` and `duplicateOf` names the original. A PDF import reports the file as `duplicate`. Duplicate detection uses Elicit ids, DOIs, and strong title similarity. Authors can corroborate a title match, and a sufficiently strong title can match without author corroboration; conflicting DOI, year, or abstract evidence can rule out a title-based match. Items in one request are also matched against each other.
- Adding sources to a collection validates all source ids before changing memberships; an unknown or inaccessible source fails that add request. Removing sources skips ids not in the collection. Do not assume every bulk operation is atomic: source saves are processed individually and PDF imports report per-file outcomes.
- Deleting a source is a soft delete. A repeat returns `204`. Deleting a collection is permanent. Its sources stay in the library. A repeat returns `404`.
- DOIs saved through the API are stored in bare lowercase form (`10.1056/nejmoa2307563`). Input and the `doi` filter accept `doi.org` URLs, `doi:` prefixes, and any letter case.
- A malformed id, or an unknown query parameter or body key, returns `400 invalid_request` with the field name.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description:
Projects: the shared workspaces that group sessions, files, and artifacts, including those shared with you.

### Conventions

- A detail endpoint returns the resource. The list endpoint returns `{ projects, nextCursor, totalCount }`. Send `nextCursor` as `cursor` to get the next page. `nextCursor` is `null` on the last page.
- You see projects you own plus any shared with you, directly or with your organization. Each carries your `role`: `owner`, `writer`, or `reader`. Readers view a project; writers also add and remove its contents; only the owner can share it or change who it is shared with.
- A project id you cannot see returns `404`, and so does one you can read but do not own when you call a share endpoint, so an id can never be probed for existence or ownership.
- Shares are keyed by email, never by user id. A recipient with an Elicit account has `status: "registered"`; an email without one gets a pending invitation and `status: "invited"`.
- Roles describe **effective** access, not stored rows. An organization-wide share only reaches its members while that organization's plan includes sharing, and a member covered by one holds the stronger of it and their own share.
- Sharing through this API grants read-only access. Edit access is granted in the Elicit web interface, which applies the organization and plan rules it requires; an email that already has it keeps it, and this endpoint reports their `role` as `writer` rather than downgrading them.
- Creating a share returns `201`. Repeating it is safe and changes nothing.
- A malformed id, or an unknown query parameter or body key, returns `400 invalid_request` with the field name.

post.description:
Search Elicit's database of over 138 million academic papers using natural language queries.

Semantic search uses natural language understanding to find relevant papers even when the exact terms don't match.

Set `corpus` to `pubmed` to restrict results to PubMed, or leave it as the default `elicit` for the full paper index. Set `searchMode` to `"keyword"` to use corpus-specific query syntax instead of natural language: Lucene-style boolean expressions for `elicit`, and PubMed syntax such as `[Title/Abstract]` and `[MeSH]` for `pubmed`.

Filters and `searchMode: "keyword"` are mutually exclusive — put any filter expressions directly into the query string when using keyword search. Mixing them returns a 400.

To search clinical trials instead, use [`POST /api/v2/search/trials`](#tag/Search/paths/~1search~1trials/post).

### Limits

`maxResults` defaults to 10. Search returns up to that many results in one response; it does not provide a pagination cursor. Each plan caps how many results a single request may return. A value above your plan's cap returns `400 invalid_request` rather than being silently reduced:

| Plan | Results per request |
|------|--------------------|
| Basic | No access |
| Plus | No access |
| Pro | 300 |
| Scale | 500 |
| Enterprise | 10,000 |

Search is rate-limited only by the global limit of 100 requests per minute per IP address, applied across all endpoints and all plans. Exceeding it returns a `429` and blocks the IP for 5 minutes.

Upgrade your plan in [account settings](https://elicit.com/settings) for higher per-request result caps.

### Example

```bash
curl -X POST https://elicit.com/api/v2/search/papers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer elk_live_your_key_here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "effects of sleep deprivation on cognitive performance"}'
```

post.description:
Start an asynchronous report generation job. Elicit will search for relevant papers, screen them for relevance, extract structured data, and produce a full research report.

Reports are long-running operations (typically 5–15 minutes). The response includes a `sessionId` and a `links.self` URL that you poll for status.

The report is also visible at the `url` returned in the response, where you can watch it progress in real time.

### Workflow

1. **POST /api/v2/sessions/reports** — submit your research question (returns immediately with `sessionId`)
2. **GET `links.self`** (`/api/v2/sessions/reports/:sessionId`) — poll while `status` is `processing`. If it becomes `pausedForInsufficientQuota`, resolve the usage limit and POST to `links.resume` before continuing.
3. When complete, use the available `pdfUrl` and `docxUrl` fields to download the report, and `txtUrl`, `bibUrl`, and `risUrl` for its reference list (APA text, BibTeX, and RIS). Check `exportsStatus` for reference-list availability; these URLs are not guaranteed to be present immediately.

### Example

```bash
# 1. Create the report
curl -X POST https://elicit.com/api/v2/sessions/reports \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer elk_live_your_key_here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"researchQuestion": "What are the effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists on cardiovascular outcomes?"}'

# 2. Poll while status is "processing"; resolve quota pauses before resuming
curl https://elicit.com/api/v2/sessions/reports/{sessionId} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer elk_live_your_key_here"
```

get.description:
Poll the status of a report created via `POST /api/v2/sessions/reports`.

### Status transitions

- **processing** — Elicit is actively searching, screening, and extracting data. You can watch progress in real time at the `url`.
- **pausedForInsufficientQuota** — The account exceeded its usage limit mid-run. The report stays paused until resumed via the `links.resume` URL (or the Elicit web interface) once the limit is resolved.
- **completed** — The report is finished. The `result` field contains the report content.
- **failed** — Something went wrong. The `error` field contains details.
- **unknown** — Status is not tracked for this report (legacy or user-created reports).

### Polling recommendation

Poll every 30–60 seconds. Reports typically complete in 5–15 minutes depending on the number of papers.

### Including the full report body

By default, `result.reportBody` and `result.abstract` are omitted to keep polling responses lightweight. To include them, add `?include=reportBody` to the request.

### Download availability

Download URLs are optional and expire after 7 days; fetch this endpoint again for fresh URLs. `exportsStatus` describes the reference-list exports (`txtUrl`, `bibUrl`, `risUrl`), not PDF/DOCX. `ready` means a cached export manifest was served, which can be stale; it does not prove that missing formats have no export. `generating` or `unavailable` means no cached downloads can be served yet.

If expected reference-list URLs are missing, wait at least 60 seconds and repeat this GET, even after `status: "completed"` and `exportsStatus: "ready"`. Cached manifests are reused for a 60-second cooldown, and older manifests can also be served during generation or upstream failures. One retry is not a freshness guarantee: use bounded retries with backoff, then report that the expected downloads remain unavailable instead of concluding they do not exist.

### Example

```bash
# Poll for status
curl https://elicit.com/api/v2/sessions/reports/{sessionId} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer elk_live_your_key_here"

# Fetch with full report body
curl "https://elicit.com/api/v2/sessions/reports/{sessionId}?include=reportBody" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer elk_live_your_key_here"
```

post.description:
Start a systematic review. Elicit runs the stages you configure — searches, abstract screening, fulltext screening, extraction, and a report. Each stage runs only when you include it; omit a stage to skip it. The default example below runs a complete review end-to-end.

Systematic reviews are long-running operations. The response includes a `sessionId` and a `links.self` URL (`/api/v2/sessions/systematic-reviews/:sessionId`) that you poll for status. You can also watch progress live at the `url` in the response.

Two options are chosen by the person requesting the review rather than by the client calling this endpoint: the screening `depth` at each stage and `extraction.useFigures`, both of which require higher usage when enabled. Set them explicitly rather than relying on the defaults — the examples below do — and check the `settings` block in the response to confirm what the review is actually running with.

### Plan limits

| Plan | Max columns | Max results per query | Max total results | Figure extraction |
|------|-------------|----------------------|-------------------|-------------------|
| Pro | 20 | 1,000 | 5,000 | No |
| Scale | 30 | 5,000 | 20,000 | Yes |
| Enterprise | 40 | 10,000 | 40,000 | Yes |

### Example

```bash
curl -X POST https://elicit.com/api/v2/sessions/systematic-reviews \
-H "Authorization: Bearer elk_live_your_key_here" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{
  "researchQuestion": "Do GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce MACE in T2D patients?",
  "searches": [{ "query": "GLP-1 cardiovascular outcomes", "maxResults": 200 }],
  "abstractScreening": { "generate": true, "depth": "thorough" },
  "fulltextScreening": { "reuseAbstractCriteria": true, "depth": "thorough" },
  "extraction": { "generate": true, "useFigures": false },
  "generateReport": true
}'
```

get.description:
Poll the status of a systematic review created via `POST /api/v2/sessions/systematic-reviews`.

### Status transitions

- **processing** — the pipeline is running. Watch progress at `url`.
- **pausedForInsufficientQuota** — the account exceeded its usage limit mid-run. The review stays paused until resumed via the `links.resume` URL (or the Elicit web interface) once the limit is resolved.
- **completed** — the pipeline finished. Stage-organized exports appear under `data`. Only stages that actually ran are included.
- **failed** — something went wrong. The `error` field contains details. `data` may still contain exports for stages that completed before the failure.
- **unknown** — status is not tracked (legacy or user-created).

### Response shape

`data` can include stage outputs before `status: "completed"`. `exportsStatus` describes cache availability, not whether every completed stage has been exported:

- `ready` — a cached export manifest was served. It can be stale and omit newly completed stages; missing URLs do not prove that a stage did not run.
- `generating` — exports are being generated and no cached downloads are available yet. Poll again later.
- `unavailable` — export generation is temporarily unavailable. Retry the GET later; this is separate from the research session's `status`.

Poll every 30–60 seconds while processing. If the session is paused for insufficient quota, resolve the usage limit and POST to `links.resume` instead of continuing to poll for completion.

**After completion, repoll for missing expected exports even when `exportsStatus` is `ready`.** Wait at least 60 seconds before fetching this endpoint again: a manifest younger than the 60-second cooldown can be served without checking newly completed stages. Older cached manifests can also be served while another request regenerates exports or when regeneration or session-state loading fails. There is no fixed freshness guarantee. Check `dataFreshness` to detect an unchanged cache, but do not treat its timestamp alone as proof that every stage is exported. Use bounded retries with backoff; if expected URLs remain missing, report incomplete export availability rather than assuming the stages never ran.

- `data.search.{csv,xlsx}` — gather-stage paper list.
- `data.screen.{csv,xlsx}` — abstract-screening results.
- `data.fulltext.{csv,xlsx}` — fulltext-screening results (only when fulltext screening is configured).
- `data.extract.{csv,xlsx}` — extraction-stage results.
- `data.report` — structured content under `result`, plus optional `pdf` / `docx` / `txt` (APA reference list) / `bib` (BibTeX) / `ris` presigned download URLs.

All stage URLs are presigned for 7 days and serve with `Content-Disposition: attachment` so browser downloads land with the canonical filename.

`dataFreshness` is the ISO timestamp of the cached export manifest used for this response, or `null` when no timestamp is available for the returned data. It is not the session's completion time or a guarantee of current exports.

### Including the full report body

By default, `data.report.result.reportBody` and `data.report.result.abstract` are omitted to keep responses light. Append `?include=reportBody` to include them.

get.description:
List all sessions — reports, systematic reviews, and research-agent sessions — for the authenticated user in a single feed, ordered by creation date (newest first).

Each item carries its `sessionId`, a `type` field (`report`, `systematicReview`, or `agent`), and a `links` object with the URLs for the item's follow-up requests: `links.self` is the typed get endpoint for its full status and results, and `links.resume` appears only while the session is paused for insufficient quota. Agent items omit `executionStage` (agent sessions have no pipeline stages); for them `status: "completed"` means idle and awaiting input rather than terminally finished.

Results are paginated using cursor-based pagination. Use the `nextCursor` value from the response to fetch the next page. Filters apply to all session types; pass `type` to list a single kind.

### Example

```bash
# First page
curl https://elicit.com/api/v2/sessions?limit=10 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer elk_live_your_key_here"

# Next page
curl "https://elicit.com/api/v2/sessions?limit=10&cursor=2025-06-15T14:30:00.000Z_5ad08bfb-cbe0-4911-a8c3-309760d33029" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer elk_live_your_key_here"

# Only reports created via the API
curl "https://elicit.com/api/v2/sessions?type=report&source=api" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer elk_live_your_key_here"
```

curl -X POST https://elicit.com/api/v2/sessions/{sessionId}/resume \

post.description:
Grant read-only access to a session by email. Works for every session type — reports, systematic reviews, and Research Agent sessions. New recipients can view the session; this grant does not let them modify, resume, stop, or re-share it.

Existing editor or reviewer permissions on reports and systematic reviews are preserved, not downgraded. The returned `share.role: "reader"` describes this API's read-only grant, not the recipient's full effective permissions. Inspect or change higher-permission roles in the web interface; they are not returned by the list-shares endpoint. **Revoking the email with DELETE still removes its direct share, including an existing editor or reviewer grant.**

If the email belongs to an existing Elicit account the share takes effect immediately (`status: "registered"`). Otherwise a pending invitation is created and an email is sent (`status: "invited"`); the share activates when they create an account.

Only the session owner can manage shares. A recipient of a shared **agent** session sees it in `GET /api/v2/sessions` with `role: "shared"`; a recipient of a shared **report** or **systematic review** opens it via the returned web-app `url` — it will **not** appear in their `GET /api/v2/sessions` list, which stays owner-only for review sessions.

curl -X POST https://elicit.com/api/v2/sessions/{sessionId}/shares \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer elk_live_your_key_here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

post.description:
Start a stateful Research Agent session. Elicit investigates the query asynchronously, reports its activity as structured events, and may produce downloadable artifacts.

The response returns immediately with a `sessionId`. Use the events endpoint to follow the research, then send messages to refine or continue it. The session is also available at the returned `url`.

### Project context

Optionally pass `projectId` to start inside an existing project you own. Find one with `GET /api/v2/projects`, or create one first with `POST /api/v2/projects` and a body such as `{"name":"GLP-1 safety review","goal":"Compare cardiovascular outcomes"}`. Then pass the returned `id` to this endpoint. MCP supports the same workflow with `list_projects`, `create_project`, and `create_agent_session`.

The session becomes a project item before its first turn starts, and the agent receives the project context from the initial query. The response includes `projectId`. Shared projects are not supported, even with writer access. A missing, removed, deleted, or non-owned project returns `400 invalid_request` before creating a session or charging workflow quota. Omission preserves standalone creation. Creating a project is a separate operation; a failed session creation leaves the project available to reuse.

### Research depth

Optionally set `researchDepth` to `fastest`, `fast`, `balanced`, `smart`, or `smartest` when creating a session (also supported by MCP's `create_agent_session`). Omission preserves the existing account/model default. The selected preset is applied through the same server-side configuration and entitlement checks as the web interface. Plan and contract limits still apply: unavailable depths are reduced to the allowed ceiling, so `smartest` becomes `smart` on Pro, and Enterprise accounts without higher-depth access are limited to `balanced`. `custom` and arbitrary model configuration are not supported. This option is only available at creation, not on follow-up messages.

### End-to-end workflow

A full research task may involve several requests against a single session. To drive it end to end:

1. **(Optional) Upload files.** POST /api/v2/files, PUT the bytes to the presigned URL, and keep each `file_id` (see the Upload endpoint).
2. **Create the session.** POST /api/v2/sessions/agents with your `query` and any `attachments`. The response is immediate with `status: "processing"` and a `sessionId`.
3. **Poll for activity.** GET /api/v2/sessions/agents/:sessionId/events. Pass the returned `cursor` unchanged on each subsequent poll to receive immutable event occurrences not observed at that checkpoint. Append them in response order and deduplicate retries by `eventId`. Poll every 3–10 seconds while the top-level `status` is `processing`.
4. **Detect idle.** The agent is ready for another request when a `session_idle` event appears and the top-level `status` returns to `completed`. For a Research Agent session, `completed` means **idle and awaiting input** — not that the session is permanently closed. Watch for these events along the way:
   - `question` — the agent needs input; answer it with a follow-up message.
   - `error` — the agent encountered an error; `retryable` indicates whether resending is worthwhile.
   - `session_paused` — the account hit its usage limit; the status becomes `pausedForInsufficientQuota`. Resolve the limit, then resume the session via POST /api/v2/sessions/:sessionId/resume (or the Elicit web interface) before continuing.
5. **Send a follow-up.** POST /api/v2/sessions/agents/:sessionId/messages with your message (and any `attachments`). Correlate the returned `messageId` with the matching `user_message` event, then return to step 3.
6. **Retrieve artifacts.** GET /api/v2/sessions/agents/:sessionId/artifacts to list what the agent produced: files appear under `artifacts` (GET .../artifacts/:artifactId/download for a short-lived presigned download URL — treat it as a credential), and interactive outputs (tables, prose, presentations, figures) appear under `deliveredOutputs` (GET .../artifacts/:artifactId/content for their contents).
7. **Retrieve cited sources.** GET /api/v2/sessions/agents/:sessionId/sources for every source the session cited, listed once each with its abstract. Join it to the citations on the events feed by `sourceRef`.
8. **(Optional) Stop early.** POST /api/v2/sessions/agents/:sessionId/stop to interrupt a running turn, then poll the events endpoint for the `session_stopped` event.

### Session status

The list, detail, and events endpoints all report the same top-level `status`:

- `processing` — the agent is working (or the session has not started yet).
- `completed` — idle and awaiting input; the latest work finished successfully.
- `failed` — the latest work ended with an error.
- `pausedForInsufficientQuota` — paused at the account usage limit; resume once the limit clears.

The shared session-status schema also includes `unknown` for legacy reports and systematic reviews. Agent endpoints return the four statuses above: when no execution outcome is available and the session is not quota-paused, they report `processing` rather than `unknown`.

Application errors use the standard `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }` envelope. The edge rate limit's `429` response is the flat format described under Error Handling.

### Example

```bash
# Minimal
curl -X POST https://elicit.com/api/v2/sessions/agents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer elk_live_your_key_here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"What are the effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists on cardiovascular outcomes?"}'

# Start inside an owned project
curl -X POST https://elicit.com/api/v2/sessions/agents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer elk_live_your_key_here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"Compare the latest trials.","projectId":"9c1f6a7e-5d24-4a3b-9f0e-1b2c3d4e5f60"}'

# Select a research depth
curl -X POST https://elicit.com/api/v2/sessions/agents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer elk_live_your_key_here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"Compare randomized trials of GLP-1 receptor agonists.","researchDepth":"smart"}'

# With an uploaded file attached to the initial turn
curl -X POST https://elicit.com/api/v2/sessions/agents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer elk_live_your_key_here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"Summarize the attached trial and compare it to the current literature.","attachments":[{"file_id":"a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d"}]}'
```

- **completed** — The agent is idle and awaiting input. This is *not* a terminal state: the session can be continued (agent sessions have no terminal "finished" state).

get.description:
Get a reduced view of a Research Agent session's activity.

Streaming text, thinking, and tool-input deltas are collapsed into complete typed entries. With no `cursor`, the response contains the full reduced history. Pass the returned cursor unchanged on the next poll to receive immutable event occurrences not observed at that checkpoint.

The public event kinds are `user_message`, `agent_message`, `methods`, `question`, `activity`, `artifacts_delivered`, `delivered_outputs`, `error`, `session_idle`, `session_paused`, `session_resumed`, `stop_requested`, and `session_stopped`. Internal tool names, sandbox paths, raw tool results, and candidate counters are never returned.

Every event includes a stable `eventId` and an ISO 8601 `createdAt` timestamp when available. Events are immutable and append-only. A resource can have several snapshots: for example, an `activity` may first be `started` and later `completed`. Those occurrences share an `activityId` but have distinct `eventId` values. Append incremental responses in response order and deduplicate retries by `eventId`.

The top-level `status` has exactly the same meaning and value as the list and detail endpoints. Lifecycle facts that are not part of the shared session status vocabulary are represented by explicit events: the agent becomes ready for more input with `session_idle`, a stop completes with `session_stopped`, and pause/resume use `session_paused`/`session_resumed`.

### Methods

A `methods` event follows the answer it describes and refers to it with `messageId`. It describes how the answer was produced: an `approach` sentence, a short `summary`, headed `sections`, the `keyJudgments` made along the way, the `searches` that were run, an `evidenceBase` summarizing the cited literature, and any `artifacts` the method produced.

`searches` is a deduplicated list of the queries that were run, in execution order. `source` is a stable corpus key rather than a display label — `academic` (Elicit's academic corpus), `pubmed`, `clinical_trials`, `press_release`, or `web`, with more possible as corpora are added. Together, `searchedAt`, `maxResults`, and the number of entries reproduce the search summary shown in the web interface. `summary` and `evidenceBase` are nullable: an answer can be described without either, and `sections`, `keyJudgments`, `searches` and `artifacts` are empty arrays rather than null when there is nothing to report. `evidenceBase.sourceCount` counts distinct sources, so it is lower than the answer's citation count whenever one source supports several citations. It counts a source as cited when a quote names it or a table row links to it in an artifact the answer produced or referenced — delivery is not the criterion — so for a session with a source-table column it can exceed the count shown on the Methods card in the web interface, which counts only quoted sources.

### Citations

Every citation carries its source inline, including `citationCount`, `fullTextAvailable`, `studyTypeTags`, `journalQuartile`, and `elicitId`. `fullTextAvailable` here reports only what the session itself recorded, so it is frequently `null`; read it from the cited-sources endpoint, which resolves the unknowns. Abstracts are not on this feed — a message is re-emitted with a new `eventId` whenever its citations change, so an abstract would be repeated on each re-emission. Fetch them once from the cited-sources endpoint instead and join on `sourceRef`, which identifies the same source everywhere it appears in a session.

### Polling example

```bash
# Full history
curl https://elicit.com/api/v2/sessions/agents/{sessionId}/events \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer elk_live_your_key_here"

# Only event occurrences not observed at the cursor checkpoint
curl "https://elicit.com/api/v2/sessions/agents/{sessionId}/events?cursor={cursor}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer elk_live_your_key_here"
```

Poll every 3–10 seconds while `status` is `processing`. The agent is ready for another request when a `session_idle` event appears and the status returns to `completed` (idle, awaiting input). A `question` event indicates that the agent needs input. A `session_stopped` event confirms that a stop request was processed. If a cursor is rejected, refetch once without a cursor and rebuild local event state.

post.description:
Stage a file so it can be attached to a Research Agent turn or imported into your library. This is a two-step, presigned upload:

1. **POST /api/v2/files** with the filename, MIME type, and exact byte size. The response returns a `file_id` and a short-lived presigned `upload_url`.
2. **PUT** the raw file bytes to `upload_url` with the same `Content-Type` and a `Content-Length` matching `size_bytes`. Do not send an `Authorization` header on the PUT — the URL is already signed.

Then either pass `{ "file_id": "..." }` in the `attachments` array of a create-session or send-message request — attached files are made available to the agent exactly as uploads made in the web interface are — or pass the `file_id` in `fileIds` to `POST /api/v2/library/imports` to parse the PDF into your library. A staged file can be claimed by one session or one library import. Once attached to a session, the same `file_id` can be referenced again in later turns of that session, including after the staging expiry; it cannot be reused in another session or import.

The request/response fields for this endpoint are deliberately `snake_case` (`content_type`, `size_bytes`, `file_id`, `upload_url`, `expires_at`), unlike the camelCase used elsewhere in the v2 surface. Files are capped at 30 MB, and a session accepts at most 100 distinct files totaling 10GB across all turns. Upload the bytes and make the first claim within 30 minutes: `upload_url` and an **unclaimed** `file_id` expire at `expires_at`. A claimed attachment is not subject to that staging expiry.

### Example

```bash
# 1. Register the upload
curl -X POST https://elicit.com/api/v2/files \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer elk_live_your_key_here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"filename":"trial-results.pdf","content_type":"application/pdf","size_bytes":245678}'

# 2. Upload the bytes to the returned upload_url
curl -X PUT "{upload_url}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/pdf" \
  --data-binary @trial-results.pdf

# 3. Attach {"file_id": "..."} to a create-session or /messages request,
#    or import it with POST /library/imports {"fileIds": ["..."]}
```
